Re.: Outcome of Board Meeting and disclosure under Regulation 30 of Schedule III of the Securities
and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015,
as amended (“Listing Regulations”) with respect to further updates in relation to the proposed
investment into Brahma AI Holdings Limited (“Brahma Holdings”) and Brahma AI Services India
Limited (“Brahma India”), material subsidiaries of the Company, by way of subscription to
compulsorily convertible preference shares (“CCPS”) of Brahma Holdings by Multiples Private
Equity Gift Fund IV and of Brahma India by Multiples Private Equity Fund IV (collectively referred
to as “Multiples”)
Dear Sir/ Madam,
This is further to our disclosure dated September 23, 2026 (“Earlier Disclosure”) in relation to the
proposed investment by Multiples in Brahma Holdings and Brahma India, material subsidiaries of Prime
Focus Limited (“Company”), respectively (“Proposed Transaction”).
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, i.e. October 15, 2026, has, inter alia,
considered the following and approved / recommended the same:
1.

Subject to the provisions of applicable laws including approval of the members of the Company in
accordance with provisions of Regulation 23(4) of the Listing Regulations, the Board considered and
recommended the following matters in relation to the Proposed Transaction:
(a)

The material related party transaction between DNEG S.à.r.l (“DNEG Parent”), an unlisted
material subsidiary of the Company and Brahma Holdings, a material unlisted subsidiary of
the Company, for entering into the Ancillary Framework Deed with Brahma Holdings, Brahma
India, Multiples, pursuant to which DNEG Parent shall, inter alia, undertake indemnity
obligations in favour of Brahma Holdings, (for itself and as agent for each Brahma Group
Company (as defined in the Framework Deed)), for any Indemnified Liability (as defined in
the Framework Deed), for such amounts as may become payable from time to time in
accordance with the Framework Deed;

(b)

The material related party transaction between Double Negative Holdings Limited (“DNEG
Holdings”), an unlisted subsidiary of the Company and Brahma Holdings, for entering into a
shareholders agreement relating to Brahma Holdings with Brahma Holdings, Multiples, and

 Mr. Prabhu Narasimhan (“SHA”) under which each shareholder of Brahma Holdings
(including DNEG Holdings) that is a party to the SHA has agreed to indemnify and hold
harmless Brahma Holdings and each Group Company (as defined in the SHA) on an after-Tax
basis from and against any liability with respect to any Tax required to be withheld, deducted
or paid on behalf of or with respect to such shareholder under applicable law, including any
interest, penalties, or costs arising therefrom; and
(c)

2.

The material related party transaction for platform license arrangement between DNEG Parent
and Brahma Holdings for inter alia licensing of Brahma AI Platform together with related
models, workflows, interfaces, documentation, updates, upgrades, releases and other
components for the annual fees which is expected to result in the transaction value exceeding
the applicable materiality thresholds under Regulation 23(4) of the Listing Regulations.

To convene an Extra Ordinary General Meeting of the members of the Company (“EOGM”) on
Saturday, November 7, 2026, through Video Conferencing / Other Audio Visual Means for and
reviewed, considered and approved the draft notice of the EOGM of the Company for:
(a) consideration and approval of the Proposed Transaction (to be read with the Earlier Disclosure)
resulting in cessation of control over Brahma Holdings and consequently, over Brahma India, the
unlisted material subsidiaries of the Company pursuant to the subscription by Multiples to CCPS of
Brahma Holdings and Brahma India, and transfer of the shares in Brahma India held by DNEG Parent
to Brahma Holdings, respectively, by way of special resolution in accordance with Regulation 24(5)
of the Listing Regulations; and (b) consideration and approval of the material related party
transactions as detailed above in Sr. No. (1).

The Meeting of the Board commenced at 7:30 p.m. and concluded at 8:15 p.m.

Sri Lotus Developers & Realty Limited, a leading Mumbai-based developer of luxury and ultra
luxury residential and commercial properties in Mumbai, with a strong focus in redevelopment &

ended 30th September 2026.
H1 FY27 has been a defining period for Sri Lotus, as the Company expands its footprint across
Mumbai’s most sought-after micro-markets while maintaining the financial discipline that
distinguishes it. Successful project launches, new redevelopment wins and steady demand for
premium homes have together driven growth alongside industry-leading profitability. With a net
debt-free balance sheet and a well-defined launch calendar for H2, the Company enters the
second half with strong momentum.

KEY BUSINESS & FINANCIAL UPDATES
❖

Pre-sales momentum: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR 470 Crs, reflecting sustained
demand for the Company’s premium offerings

❖

Pipeline additions: Three new projects secured in Q2, Lotus Supremus (Juhu), Lotus
Empressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and additional area secured for
Lotus Insignia which together adds INR 2,700-2,800 Crs of GDV

❖

H2 FY27 launches: Four projects, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, Lotus Odyssey and Lotus
Aurelia are lined up with a combined estimated GDV of ~INR 3,500-4,000 Crs, positioning
the Company well to meet its FY27 guidance

KEY FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS for Q2 FY27
❖ Pre-sales grew 83% YoY to ₹470 crore from ₹257 crore.
❖ Total Revenue grew 53% YoY to ₹269 crore from ₹176 crore
❖ EBITDA grew 113% YoY to ₹107 crore from ₹50 crore. EBITDA Margin stood at 39.9%

attention an operational clarification concerning an inadvertent communication transmitted earlier today,
October 14, 2026.

execution subject to Board approval, an unapproved working draft a email for the proposed Postal Ballot Notice
was shared with the e-voting service provider, strictly for advance configuration, system testing, and operational
readiness purposes.
Due to an unintended operational lapse at the service provider’s end arising from an administrative
miscommunication between the teams regarding test parameters, the said unapproved draft communication was
prematurely and inadvertently dispatched to shareholders today, October 14, 2026, without the authorization,
concurrence, or final clearance of the Company.

 Only an electronic mail containing indicative/test links and reference to a draft postal ballot notice was
prematurely circulated by the service provider, which has neither been approved by the Board of Directors
nor uploaded on the website of the Company or submitted to the Stock Exchange as a sanctioned notice.

by the Board of Directors of the Company.

matter at the scheduled Board Meeting on October 16, 2026.

under Section 110 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with the applicable rules, and carries no legal force.

remain strictly suppressed, disable, inactive, and recalled. The Company is in the process of issuing a direct

Subject: Update – Approval of Acquisition of Equity Shares of Stilonn Valves and

Company
Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Schedule III of the Securities and Exchange Board of
India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we wish to
inform you that the Board of Directors of Aeroflex Neu Limited, the Material Subsidiary of
the Company, at its meeting held on October 15, 2026, has, inter alia, approved acquisition
of 7,27,040 equity shares of Stilonn Valves and Controls Private Limited ("Stilonn"),
Company engaged in the business of manufacturing of precision engineering products in the
high-growth AI Infra and Data Centre space along with critical pharmaceutical and
healthcare sector, including valves, sanitary fittings and allied goods, for an aggregate
consideration of ₹16,00,21,504/- (Rupees Sixteen Crore Twenty-One Thousand Five
Hundred and Four Only). The acquisition shall be undertaken in one or more tranches
through a combination of purchase of equity shares from the existing shareholders of Stilonn
and subscription to additional equity shares proposed to be issued by Stilonn, pursuant to
the execution of a Share Purchase Agreement, Share Subscription and Shareholders'
Agreement and such other ancillary Transaction Documents as may be necessary.
Consequent to the completion of the proposed acquisition, the shareholding of Aeroflex Neu
Limited in Stilonn shall stand at 51.01% of its issued and paid-up equity share capital,
thereby resulting in Stilonn becoming a Subsidiary of Aeroflex Neu Limited.
This acquisition forms part of Aeroflex Neu Limited’s initiative in the AI Infra and Data
Centre sector and in establishing an integrated platform for high-tech and critical
engineering solutions.

 It is further informed that, Aeroflex Neu Limited has made the requisite disclosure regarding

said, “India is witnessing one of the largest wealth creation opportunities in its history, and
technology is making financial services more accessible than ever before. We believe the next
decade will belong to platforms that combine innovation, trust and execution at scale.

Angel One is evolving into an AI-powered financial platform designed to serve clients across
trading and investing, wealth, credit and global markets. Every product we build, every capability
we add and every investment we make is guided by a simple objective: helping clients make better
financial decisions and achieve their aspirations.
Our ambition is to build a platform that becomes an indispensable part of every client's financial
journey. With strong foundations, multiple growth engines and a relentless focus on client
outcomes, we are confident in our ability to create enduring value while contributing meaningfully
to India's financial future.

Commenting on Angel One’s performance, Mr. Ambarish Kenghe, Group CEO said, “The second
quarter reinforced the resilience of our client franchise despite significant changes in India’s
market structure including revised bank funding norms and introduction of the Closing Auction
Session in cash equities. While these changes temporarily impacted broking activity, client
engagement recovered steadily, with our average daily orders reaching 5.8 million in September
2026, approaching pre-CAS levels. More importantly participation deepened as our average client
funding book reached a record high of ₹ 74.5 billion, growing by 40.5% year-on-year.
Customer preference remained strong across our platform. We increased our share of retail equity
derivatives turnover to 22.1%, up 43 basis points year-on-year, while commodity turnover more
than doubled.
We continue to evolve our platform into a broader financial-services ecosystem. During the
quarter, we began the early beta of Loan Against Securities within our NBFC and will scale the
product with discipline and responsibility. Supported by our AI and ML-powered underwriting and
risk models, monthly credit distribution reached a record high in September 2026. We also
received authorization to operate as a Global Access Provider in the IFSC, creating a pathway to
offer customers investment opportunities beyond domestic markets.

Combined with a standalone operating margin of 48.9%, above our guided range, these
investments position us well to deepen customer relationships across investing, borrowing and
wealth creation, while capitalizing on India’s long-term financialization opportunity.”

Mumbai, October 15, 2026: Megamont Limited (BSE: 523888), a diversified global commodity trading company,
has secured an import contract valued at approximately ¥2.13 crore for Pigeon Peas (Tur/Arhar), to be sourced
from Mozambique or Malawi in Africa.
The contract marks another step in the Company's strategy to diversify its commodity portfolio and expand its
presence in India's agricultural supply chain, with the objective of supplying essential agricultural commodities to
domestic FMCG companies, food processors and institutional buyers.

Supporting India's Domestic Agricultural Supply Chain
Pigeon Peas are among India's widely consumed pulses and form an important part of the country's staple food
basket. International sourcing plays a complementary role in supporting domestic availability and meeting the
requirements of India's food-processing and consumption markets.
Through this transaction, Megamont aims to leverage its global sourcing capabilities to establish reliable
procurement channels for essential agricultural commodities, while strengthening its participation in India's
domestic food supply chain.
The Company intends to market the imported Pigeon Peas to FMCG manufacturers, food-processing companies
and other institutional customers, supporting its strategy of developing long-term relationships across
consumption-driven industries.

Favourable Policy Environment Aligns with Megamont's Long-Term Vi

on

The Government of India has extended the free import policy for Tur/Pigeon Peas until March 31, 2027,
supporting continued international sourcing of the commodity to supplement domestic supplies.
This policy environment aligns with Megamont's broader vision of establishing a Global Multi-Product Trading
House, connecting key commodity-producing regions with major consumption markets across geographies.
By expanding its international sourcing network and diversifying into essential commodities, Megamont aims to
build a scalable trading platform serving multiple industries and markets.
The Company's strategy also focuses on identifying commercial arbitrage opportunities arising from differences
in international commaodity prices, sourcing costs and domestic market demand, while maintaining disciplined
trade execution and risk management.

Strengthening Global Sourcing and Market Reach
®

The contract provides for sourcing Pigeon Peas from Mozambique or Malawi, expanding Megamont's
participation in African agricultural trade corridors.

®

Shipments are scheduled between November and December 2026, with delivery at Nhava Sheva Port, India.

®

The transaction complements Megamont's existing presence across metals, energy, industrial commodities
and agricultural products, further advancing its strategy of building a diversified global trading business.

persons belonging to the ‘Promoter & Promoter Group’ Category to ‘Public’ Category under Regulation 31A of

does not exercise control over the affairs of the Company, directly or indirectly. Also, as on the date of receipt of

in the Company and does not possess any kind of special rights in the Company. The Board also noted that the
Outgoing Promoter neither represents the board of directors (including as a nominee director) of the Company nor
is acting as a Key Managerial Person in the Company. The Board also noted that the Outgoing Promoter is neither
a ‘wilful defaulter’ as per the Reserve Bank of India Guidelines nor a fugitive economic offender.
Furthermore, the Board noted that the outgoing promoter has entered into a Family Settlement Agreement dated
September 20, 2026 with Mohammad Kamil Qureshi, Zulfiqar Ahmad Qurashi, Mohammad Ashraf
Qureshi, Mohammad Mehmood Qureshi and Gulzar Ahmad (the existing Promoters of the Company),

Qurashi, Mohammad Ashraf Qureshi, Mohammad Mehmood Qureshi and Gulzar Ahmad will continue as
the promotors of the Company.

as required under Regulation 38 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
and the proposed reclassification is not being initiated for achieving the Minimum Public Shareholding. The
trading in the shares of the company has not been suspended by the Stock Exchanges. The Company does not
have any outstanding due to the SEBI, the Stock Exchanges or Depositories.

dated September 20, 2026 and in accordance with the provisions of Regulation 31A of the Listing Regulations,
